classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|XPHB|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Demon Hunter spells, which appear in the {@filter Demon Hunter spell list|spells|class=Demon Hunter (wow:s)} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Demon Hunter Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two {@filter level 1 Demon Hunter spells|spells|class=Demon Hunter (wow:s)|level=1}. {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} and {@spell Ensnaring Strike|XPHB} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Demon Hunter levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Demon Hunter Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Demon Hunter spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Demon Hunter Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Demon Hunter, your list of prepared spells can include six Demon Hunter spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Demon Hunter feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Demon Hunter spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one spell on your list with another Demon Hunter spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Demon Hunter spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} (not a {@item Druidic Focus|XPHB}) as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Demon Hunter spells.

classFeature.name: Favored Enemy
entries: You always have the {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
The number of times you can cast the spell without a spell slot increases when you reach certain Demon Hunter levels, as shown in the Favored Enemy column of the Demon Hunter Features table.

classFeature.name: Death Coil
entries: Your creature type becomes Undead.
You also gain the ability to manipulate negative energy. You have a pool of d8s to fuel this ability. The number of dice in the pool equals one plus your Charisma modifier (minimum of one die).

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can target a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself and force it to make a Constitution saving throw, expending dice from the pool. The maximum number of dice you can expend at once equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of one die). Roll the dice you expend. The target takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. If the target is an Undead, you can choose to have it regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll's total instead. Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Demon Hunter
entries: {@i Embrace the Magic of Demons to Fight Fire with Fire}

Most Demon Hunters joined Illidan on Outland as he marshaled his forces to battle the Burning Legion. You might have followed a different path, inspired by Illidan rather than directly trained by him, but the result is the same: You have embraced the magic of the Burning Legion with the singular goal of defeating it on Azeroth and every other world.

entries.name: Hero Classes
entries: Three of the World of Warcraft classes—{@class Death Knight|WarcraftStreamlined}, {@class Demon Hunter|WarcraftStreamlined}, and {@class Evoker|WarcraftStreamlined}—are hero classes, meaning that they are typically available only to characters starting at level 3 or higher. In the story of World of Warcraft, characters with these classes are already experienced and powerful adventurers by the time they enter the game.

entries.name: Playing a Demon Hunter
entries: Demon hunter is a hero class, which means you typically must start play at level 3 or higher (see the "Hero Classes" sidebar earlier in this chapter).
All demon hunters in World of Warcraft lore are elves (blood elves, night elves, or void elves), so check with your DM before playing a demon hunter of another species.
As a Demon Hunter, you can choose one of three specializations: Devourer, Havoc, or Vengeance.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Fragments
entries: You harvest the energy of souls to fuel some of your special powers. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you gain a number of soul fragments equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one fragment); each soul fragment is a Tiny object in the form of a crystal. These fragments last until you finish another {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, at which point they disintegrate. If you ever move more than 30 feet from a fragment, the fragment immediately teleports to you, appearing somewhere on your person.
If a soul fragment effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your Demon Hunter spell save DC.

The number of soul fragments you gain when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} increases when you reach Demon Hunter levels 13 (Wisdom modifier plus one soul fragment) and 17 (Wisdom modifier plus two soul fragments).

entries.name: Using Soul Fragments
entries: You can use soul fragments in the following ways:

items.name: Double Jump
items.entry: You can expend one soul fragment to cast {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} or {@spell Jump|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.

items.name: Soul Cleave
items.entry: Once on each of your turns, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can expend one soul fragment and replace one of your attacks with a whirlwind of soul energy. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Psychic damage equal to 1d12 plus your Wisdom modifier, and you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Regaining Soul Fragments
entries: When an enemy you can see within 30 feet of you dies, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain one expended soul fragment.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Sight
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Torment
entries: A creature marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} spell has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against targets other than you.

Additionally, once per turn when you hit a creature marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} with an attack roll with a weapon or a Demon Hunter spell, you can impose one of the following effects on the target (your choice):

items.name: Aura of Pain
items.entry: The target subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn.

items.name: Chaos Strike
items.entry: The target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Illidari Knowledge
entries: You gain new mastery over souls, granting you new ways to use {@subclassFeature Soul Fragments|Demon Hunter|WarcraftStreamlined|Devourer|WarcraftStreamlined|3}:

items.name: Disrupt
items.entry: You can expend two {@subclassFeature Soul Fragments|Demon Hunter|WarcraftStreamlined|Devourer|WarcraftStreamlined|3} to cast {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} in response to that spell's trigger, using your spellcasting ability.

items.name: Warglaive Mastery
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one {@subclassFeature Soul Fragments|Demon Hunter|WarcraftStreamlined|Devourer|WarcraftStreamlined|3||Soul Fragment} to cast {@spell Throw Glaive|WarcraftStreamlined} without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Shatter
entries: Your mastery of fel magic reaches new heights. When you use the Soul Cleave option of {@subclassFeature Soul Fragments|Demon Hunter|WarcraftStreamlined|Devourer|WarcraftStreamlined|3}, the damage increases to {@damage 2d12} plus your Wisdom modifier.

In addition, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you regain one {@subclassFeature Soul Fragments|Demon Hunter|WarcraftStreamlined|Devourer|WarcraftStreamlined|3||Soul Fragment} if you have none.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Fragments
entries: You harvest the energy of souls to fuel some of your special powers. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you gain a number of soul fragments equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one fragment); each soul fragment is a Tiny object in the form of a crystal. These fragments last until you finish another {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, at which point they disintegrate. If you ever move more than 30 feet from a fragment, the fragment immediately teleports to you, appearing somewhere on your person.
If a soul fragment effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your Demon Hunter spell save DC.

The number of soul fragments you gain when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} increases when you reach Demon Hunter levels 13 (Wisdom modifier plus one soul fragment) and 17 (Wisdom modifier plus two soul fragments).

subclassFeature.name: Runeforging
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can inscribe one of the following runes on a melee weapon you are holding, or you can transfer the rune to a different weapon. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace it with a different rune.

entries.name: Blood
entries: When you inscribe this rune on your weapon, and whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} while the rune is inscribed on your weapon, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Death Knight level. While you are wielding your inscribed weapon, you gain these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} whenever you reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Frost
entries: While you are wielding your inscribed weapon, damage from your weapon attacks, Death Knight spells, and Death Knight features ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. When you make the extra attack of the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property and hit while wielding your inscribed weapon, you deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage.

entries.name: Unholy
entries: While you are wielding your inscribed weapon, damage from your weapon attacks, Death Knight spells, and Death Knight features ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. If your inscribed weapon has the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} property, the first creature you hit with it each turn takes extra Necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

subclassFeature.name: Runic Power
entries: Immediately after you cast {@spell Rune Strike|WarcraftStreamlined}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to gain one of the following benefits based on the rune inscribed on your weapon.

entries.name: Blood
entries: You regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Necrotic damage dealt with your {@spell Rune Strike|WarcraftStreamlined}.

entries.name: Frost
entries: Frost covers your weapon and shatters on impact. The target of your {@spell Rune Strike|WarcraftStreamlined} and each enemy in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target take {@damage 2d6} Cold damage.

entries.name: Unholy
entries: The target of your {@spell Rune Strike|WarcraftStreamlined} is cursed until the end of your next turn. The next time the cursed target makes a saving throw, it subtracts {@dice 1d6} from the roll, and the curse ends.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Deathly Endurance
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold, Necrotic, and Psychic damage while in your Aura of Protection.

subclassFeature.name: Runic Mastery
entries: You can invoke the power of the rune inscribed on your weapon. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The effect depends on the rune you have inscribed.

entries.name: Blood
entries: When a creature hits another creature you can see within 10 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage the target takes by your Death Knight level. You then lose a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Death Knight level.

entries.name: Frost
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one attack with an exhalation of frost magic in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in that area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature takes {@damage 8d6} Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Unholy
entries: When you cast {@spell Summon Undead|XPHB}, you can modify it so that the spell doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting, and when summoned, the {@creature Undead Spirit|XPHB} has a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Death Knight level plus your Charisma modifier. In addition, the first time each turn the spirit hits a creature, the spirit deals extra Necrotic damage equal to half your Death Knight level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Aspect of the Horsemen
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Generate Runic Power
entries: You can restore a use of your Runic Mastery by expending a level 4 spell slot (no action required).

entries.name: Runeforging
entries: When you use your Runic Power and Runic Mastery features, you can choose any effect, not just the one that corresponds to the rune inscribed on your weapon.

entries.name: Orc
entries: Orcs originate from the planet of Draenor, and as such their primordial history is separate from the efforts of the titan Pantheon to preserve Azeroth's Worldsoul from corruption. Orcs descend from Grond, a living mountain shaped by the titan Aggramar to battle the massive botanical hivemind of the Evergrowth, which dominated ancient Draenor. Infused with life, the broken pieces that fell from Grond's body became creatures in their own right—first the mighty earth giants called colossi, then the magma giants called magnaron, then the fearsome gronn, then ogron, and finally, from the ogron came ogres and orcs. Though the orcs are the smallest and weakest of Grond's descendants, they possess a fierce intellect and strong sense of community.

Some early orcs were drawn to the site of Grond's demise, and there they learned about the elemental spirits of air, earth, fire, and water. Cultivating harmony among the four elements, these orcs became the first shaman, who rose to become the spiritual leaders of their people.

In the decades before the opening of the Dark Portal, the demon lord Kil'jaeden manipulated Ner'zhul, one of the spiritual leaders of the orcs of Draenor, and through him the rest of the orc clans. Kil'jaeden convinced Ner'zhul that the draenei were conspiring against the orcs and goaded him into attacking the draenei. When Ner'zhul balked at an all-out assault on Shattrath City, Kil'jaeden discarded him and turned to Ner'zhul's apprentice, Gul'dan, who was all too eager to wreak destruction across the world in exchange for the power offered by the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}. Gul'dan gave the leaders of the orc tribes demon blood to drink, transforming them and their followers into a merciless, destructive force bound to the Legion's service.

After defeating the draenei and sating their bloodlust with internecine warfare, the orcs were lured to the world of Azeroth and enticed to make war on the human kingdoms of Stormwind and Lordaeron in what became known as the First and Second Wars. Though the Horde nearly succeeded in annihilating humanity, the Horde ultimately devoured itself from within and collapsed. The defeated orcs spent many years in internment camps, listless and lethargic without access to the fel magic that had empowered them. After many years, a visionary young warchief named {@creature Thrall|WoW} rose to lead his people in their darkest hour. Under his rule, the orcs freed themselves from the chains of demonic corruption and embraced their ancient heritage.

Thrall led his people away from human lands to the continent of Kalimdor. There, Thrall and the Horde came face to face with their old oppressor, the Burning Legion. With the aid of humans and night elves, the orcs repelled the Legion and set out to find their own path in their adopted world. The orcs claimed the harsh wastelands of Durotar as their kingdom in Kalimdor.

Now based in the city of Orgrimmar, the orcs look forward to a shining new future. With the death of the pit lord Mannoroth, whose blood brought the demonic curse on the orcs of Draenor, the curse is now lifted, and the orcs are free of demonic influence. Though they are no longer driven by dreams of conquest, they stand ready to destroy all who would challenge their sovereignty or their supremacy. It is every orc's duty to crush the enemies of Durotar, both seen and unseen, for the nefarious agents of the Burning Legion still wander the land.
Exposure to the fel magic of the Burning Legion transformed the orcs of Draenor, turning their skin green. Though the orcs of Azeroth are now free of fel corruption, they retain this green skin.

entries.name: Mag'har Orcs
entries: A few orcs were never tainted by fel magic, remaining uncorrupted—in Orcish, "mag'har." Retaining their original brown or gray skin, they also preserve the shamanistic traditions the orcs cherished before the Burning Legion's intervention.

entries.name: Human
entries: Humans are descended from the vrykul of Northrend, who are in turn the result of the {@book Old Gods'|WoW|6|Old Gods} curse of flesh taking hold of the titan-forged iron vrykul. Born small and weak as a result of the curse, humans were often killed by their vrykul parents, but some parents took the children to Lordaeron, where the humans formed scattered tribes and, under pressure from the expanding Amani empire of trolls, eventually united into the Empire of Arathor.

After several centuries, the prosperous city-states of Arathor split into the Seven Kingdoms: Alterac, Dalaran, Gilneas, Kul Tiras, Lordaeron, Stromgarde, and Stormwind far to the south. After orcs from Draenor opened the Dark Portal and invaded Azeroth, Stormwind was destroyed, and the survivors fled north. The leaders of the Seven Kingdoms united as the Alliance of Lordaeron to battle the orcs, alongside the dwarves and gnomes of Khaz Modan and the high elves of Quel'Thalas. After the Second War, humans rebuilt Stormwind City—a testament to perseverance in the face of disaster.

The kingdom of Lordaeron suffered a near-fatal blow with the coming of the plague of undeath, which killed countless people and transformed them into mindless undead servants of the Scourge. The lands once claimed by Lordaeron are now the Plaguelands, and few remnants of the human empire's glories remain.

With Lordaeron and Alterac fallen, the magocracy of Dalaran removed from the Eastern Kingdoms and then destroyed, and Gilneas afflicted with the curse of the {@race worgen|WoW}, Stormwind stands now as the strongest bastion of humanity on Azeroth and the most powerful force in the Alliance. Kul Tiras has rejoined the Alliance, and Stromgarde struggles to rebuild its strength after years of conflict against the Horde, {@book the Scourge|WoW|6|The Scourge}, and a group of ruffians called the Syndicate.

entries.name: Stormwind
entries: Law-abiding humans of the kingdom of Stormwind (whose holdings extend across Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains) hold fast to the principles of honor and justice as they defend their settlements and the Alliance against aggressors. But countless other humans engage in banditry, plot rebellion, or scheme with sinister forces such as the Cult of the Damned to bring about the end of the world.

entries.name: Kul Tiras
entries: The Admiralty of Kul Tiras is known for its strong seafaring tradition, its legendary naval fleet, and its far-reaching merchant ships. After the Third War, Lord Admiral Daelin Proudmoore led the Kul Tiran fleet in an invasion of Durotar, which led to his death. Following that tragedy, Kul Tiras withdrew from all involvement in the outside world. In its isolation, a civil war brewed as two of the four ruling houses conspired against a third, House Proudmoore. At the same time, the powerful tidesages of the isles were corrupted by the influence of the Old Gods. As the Alliance entered the Fourth War against the Horde, it sent emissaries in an effort to bring Kul Tiras back into the Alliance. Only after its internal conflicts were resolved did Kul Tiras, now under the leadership of Lord Admiral {@creature Jaina Proudmoore|WoW}, support the Alliance.

entries.name: Dalaran
entries: Dalaran was founded during the height of the Empire of Arathor and eventually became a haven for mages and a center of magical learning. Governed by the mages of the Kirin Tor, Dalaran attracted scholars and spellcasters from across the Eastern Kingdoms. During the Third War, the Scourge razed Dalaran, but in the war's aftermath, the survivors rebuilt the city. During the war against the Lich King, the Kirin Tor used mighty magic to levitate the city high in the air where no ground assault could ever reach it again and positioned it in the skies over Crystalsong Forest in Northrend. Since then, it was relocated multiple times—first above Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, then to the Broken Isles, then above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar, where it was destroyed. The survivors of that final attack are now settled in Dornogal, and the Kirin Tor (see {@book chapter 4|WoW|4|Kirin Tor}) remains a powerful force in the defense of Azeroth from all threats.

entries.name: Stromgarde
entries: During the Fourth War, descendants of the fallen kingdom of Stromgarde rebuilt their old capital in the Arathi Highlands, Stromgarde Keep, and their long-exiled king reclaimed his throne. Though the Horde fought bitterly to prevent it, the Alliance ultimately claimed victory and regained this important foothold in Lordaeron.

entries.name: Arathi Empire
entries: Centuries ago, a group of humans from the city-states of Arathor and a group of high elves from Quel'Thalas launched an exploratory expedition across the Storming Sea. In an unknown land far to the east, they founded a new Arathi Empire. The modern inhabitants of this empire all share mixed human and elf descent, calling themselves simply Arathi rather than human or elf. Most of them look predominantly human except for their slightly pointed ears. The official religion of the Arathi Empire is the church of the Sacred Flame, a fiery expression of the Holy Light, and the divine emperor rules with the aid of prophetic visions. After years of isolation from the nations of Azeroth, a group of Arathi recently came to Khaz Algar in service to one of the emperor's visions, and they have made contact with their long-sundered kin there.

entries.name: Human Renown
entries: Your starting Renown Score with {@book Stormwind|WoW|4|Stormwind Renown Perks} ({@book Alliance|WoW|4|Alliance Renown Perks}) begins at 3, but if you hail from the Arathi Empire, you have no starting Renown Score.

images.title: The descendants of the Seven Kingdoms still find much to unite them.

entries.name: Draenei
entries: Long ago, on the world of Argus, the magically gifted people called eredar drew the attention of Sargeras, the Destroyer of Worlds. Sargeras offered untold power to the three leaders of the eredar—Kil'jaeden, Archimonde, and Velen—in exchange for their unquestioning loyalty. A troubling vision soon came to Velen, who saw the eredar transformed into unspeakable demons as members of the {@book Burning Legion|WoW|6|Burning Legion}, a force that would grow immense and decimate all life. Despite Velen's warnings, Kil'jaeden and Archimonde accepted Sargeras's offer. Velen despaired at his former friends' decision and prayed for help. To his surprise and relief, he was answered by the benevolent naaru. These energy beings had, like Velen, foreseen the formation of the Legion.

The naaru offered to shepherd Velen and his followers to safety. Velen quietly gathered eredar who seemed trustworthy. As Sargeras came to Argus and transformed many willing eredar into demons, Velen and his followers narrowly escaped their home world. Furious, Kil'jaeden vowed to track Velen to the ends of creation. Even as the Burning Legion chased Velen across the cosmos, the naaru instructed the exiles, now dubbed draenei (or "exiled ones"), in the way of the Light. Deeply affected, the draenei vowed to honor the Light and uphold the naaru's ideals. In time the draenei settled on a remote world and met the orcs who inhabited it. The draenei came to call their new home Draenor or "Exiles' Refuge."

Kil'jaeden eventually learned of the idyllic world and its unsuspecting inhabitants. Working through the shaman Ner'zhul, the demon lord corrupted the orcs, who began slaughtering the peaceful draenei. When Ner'zhul refused to serve the Legion's agenda past a certain point, Kil'jaeden turned to Ner'zhul's apprentice, Gul'dan, who worked the orcs into a frenzy of bloodlust. The orc campaign against the draenei was brutally effective. Over eighty percent of the draenei population was destroyed, though a small group of survivors remained.

Velen and most of the remaining draenei survivors eventually gained control of a dimensional ship called the {@i Exodar} and used it to escape to Azeroth. In the Alliance, they found aid in their battle against the Burning Legion.

entries.name: Krokul
entries: The draenei known as Krokul (which means "Broken" in the Draenei language) are remnants of the original eredar who were neither preserved by the naaru, as the draenei were, nor transformed into demons, as the man'ari eredar were, but were corrupted by fel energies. Some of these Krokul never left their original home world of Argus, others remain on the shattered remnants of Draenor (now called Outland), and a few entered Azeroth.

entries.name: Lightforged Draenei
entries: When Velen and the draenei left their home world of Argus, they traveled from world to world for millennia to avoid Kil'jaeden and the Burning Legion. Eventually, some draenei decided to stop fleeing and take the fight back to the Legion. Led by the naaru Xe'ra, these draenei formed the Grand Army of the Light, which grew over time to include many other foes of the Burning Legion. The draenei most committed to this crusade underwent a ritual to become Lightforged, infusing their bodies with the essence of the Holy Light. Their appearance transformed to reflect this essence: Their eyes turned golden, and their bodies were marked with glowing golden tattoos.

entries.name: Man'ari Eredar
entries: The man'ari eredar are those who followed Kil'jaeden and Archimonde and joined the Burning Legion, becoming demons. After the imprisonment of Sargeras at the end of the Burning Legion's third invasion of Azeroth, a group of these eredar, called the Penitents, sought to atone for their vast misdeeds. This group's leader, Arzaal, appealed to Prophet Velen—not for forgiveness, but for an opportunity to demonstrate the sincerity of the eredar's repentance. Arzaal proved himself by returning a powerful artifact of the naaru to Velen's safekeeping. Now some of these Penitents cooperate with their draenei kin in service to the Alliance.

entries.name: Draenei Renown
entries: If you choose the draenei or Lightforged draenei Eredar Lineage, your Renown Score with the {@book Exodar|WoW|4|Exodar Renown Perks} ({@book Alliance|WoW|4|Alliance Renown Perks}) begins at 3. Otherwise, you have no starting Renown Score.

images.title: Many draenei cherish the lore collected during their long sojourn from their home world.

spell.name: Summon Deathcharger
entries: You summon an otherworldly being that appears as a loyal steed in an unoccupied space of your choice within range. This creature uses the {@creature Deathcharger|WarcraftRevised} stat block. If you already have a steed from this spell, the steed is replaced by the new one.

The steed resembles a Large, rideable animal of your choice, such as a horse, a camel, a dire wolf, or an elk. Whenever you cast the spell, choose the steed's creature type—Fiend or Undead—which determines certain traits in the stat block.

entries.name: Combat
entries: The steed is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, it shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, and it functions as a controlled mount while you ride it (as defined in the rules on {@book mounted combat|XPHB|1|Mounted Combat}). If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the steed takes its turn immediately after yours and acts independently, focusing on protecting you.

entries.name: Disappearance of the Steed
entries: The steed disappears if it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or if you die. When it disappears, it leaves behind anything it was wearing or carrying. If you cast this spell again, you decide whether you summon the steed that disappeared or a different one.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: Use the spell slot's level for the spell's level in the stat block.

spell.name: Consume Soul
entries: You drain the essence from a creature within range, which makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 4d4} Force damage, and you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the Force damage dealt. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Soul Reap
entries: You cut a hole in the fabric of reality, sending a bolt of cosmic matter toward a creature in range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target, which gains no benefit from {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} or {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}. On a hit, you deal {@damage 6d6} Force damage.

If you roll a 6 on a {@dice d6} for this spell, you can roll another {@dice d6} and add it to the damage. When you cast this spell, the maximum number of these d6s you can add to the spell's damage equals your spellcasting ability modifier.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Metamorphosis

m.text: one soul fragment, which the spell consumes

entries: Uttering an incantation, you draw on fel or Void magic to transform yourself, taking on demonic features. You gain one of the following benefits of your choice until the spell ends:

items.name: Devourer
entries: When you roll damage for a spell, weapon, or feature that deals Force damage, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3.

items.name: Havoc
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack roll using a Melee weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Fire damage.

items.name: Vengeance
entries: You have a +2 bonus to AC, and your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum and your current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} increase by 5 for the spell's duration.

spell.name: Demon Spikes
entries: You surge with fel power and sprout hard, jagged spikes. You gain a +2 bonus to AC for the duration, and when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack roll, it takes 10 Piercing damage.

spell.name: Sigil of Flame
entries: You inscribe a sigil in the air that then appears on a creature you can see within range. The target makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 2d8} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Whether or not the target fails its saving throw, it radiates heat in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from itself until the end of its next turn. At the start of the target's next turn, the target and each creature in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage (both initial and later) increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Fiery Brand
entries: You magically place a fiery demonic symbol on a creature within range, which makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d10} Fire damage and is cursed. While it remains cursed, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage it deals. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.
A cursed creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

spell.name: Eye Beam
entries: You concentrate your magic into your eyes. When you cast the spell, and as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your subsequent turns for the duration, you can unleash a burst of fel magic. Each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Throw Glaive
entries: You create a demonic warglaive and hurl it at a creature or object in range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} Slashing damage plus {@damage 1d8} Fire damage, and the glaive ricochets to a different target of your choice within 30 feet of the target. Make new attack and damage rolls against the new target.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Fire damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 1. The glaive ricochets a maximum number of times equal to the level of the slot expended; a creature can be targeted only once by each casting of this spell.

spell.name: Infernal Strike
entries: You jump through the air without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} and land in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} Fire damage and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than you until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Fel Rush
entries: Fiery fel magic surrounds you and grants you explosive speed. Until the end of your turn, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 30 feet, and your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

When you move within 5 feet of a creature or an object that isn't being worn or carried, it makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d6} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature or object can take this damage only once per turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Sigil of Chains
entries: A sigil appears at a point on the ground you can see within range, then erupts in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 5d6} Force damage, is pulled up to 10 feet straight toward the sigil, and has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.

spell.name: Collapsing Star
entries: You channel Void energy into a cataclysmic blast that fills a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point you can see within range. Each creature of your choice within the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 4d12} Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

spell.name: Chaos Nova
entries: Chaos energy bursts out in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. Each creature of your choice in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} takes {@damage 2d6} Force damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

spell.name: Rune Strike

time.condition: which you take immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

entries: The target takes an extra {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage. The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} if the target is a Celestial.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Bonestorm
entries: You conjure a whirl of battering bone and gore around yourself. You regain {@dice 4d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw. A target takes {@damage 4d8} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

spell.name: Remorseless Winter
entries: You drain the warmth from nearby creatures. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 6d6} Cold damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Whether or not a creature succeeds on its saving throw, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 10 feet until the end of its next turn as clinging frost hinders its movement.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Leeching Strike

time.condition: which you take immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

entries: The target hit by the strike takes an extra {@damage 3d8} Necrotic damage from the attack, and you regain {@dice 3d4} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8}, and the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you regain increase by {@dice 1d4}, for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Frostscythe
entries: Sweeping your weapon before you, you unleash a blast of icy cold. Each creature in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 3d8} Cold damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet for 1 minute. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Death and Decay
entries: Corruption ripples out in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} from a point on the ground you can see within range. Each creature in that area makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage and is cursed until the end of your next turn. If you deal damage to a cursed target with an attack roll, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

spell.name: Vampiric Blood
entries: For the duration, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by 10. In addition, whenever you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you regain an extra {@dice 1d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The additional healing increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Scourge Strike

time.condition: which you take immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

entries: The target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage from the attack, and it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the spell ends. At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Death Grip
entries: You harness runic energies to bind a foe to you. One creature you can see within range must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pulled straight toward you to the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

spell.name: Chains of Ice
entries: You create chains of ice around a creature you can see within range. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 1d10} Cold damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Flawed Reconstruction
entries: You stitch together the wounds of a creature you touch, which regains {@dice 3d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. However, the mending is imperfect, and the target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by {@dice 1d6}, to a minimum of 1.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The healing increases by {@dice 2d6} and the reduction increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Flawed Resurrection

components.m: a drop of blood, a piece of flesh, and a pinch of bone dust

entries: You touch a dead Humanoid that has dead been no longer than 10 days and revive it as an intelligent Undead creature. The creature returns to life with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}. This spell closes all mortal wounds, but it doesn't restore missing body parts.

The creature's type becomes Undead and it gains {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. It doesn't need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe, though it must still rest for 8 hours to gain the benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

The Undead body deteriorates over time. Whenever the creature finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum permanently decreases by 1. The creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum can only be restored by the {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell. If the creature dies and is later targeted by {@spell Resurrection|XPHB} or similar magic, it can be returned to life with its original creature type.

spell.name: Word of Terror
entries: You recite a word of fear to a creature you can see within range, which makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Dead Fog
entries: A 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of necromantic fog appears centered on a point you can see within range. The fog lasts for the duration or until strong wind (such as the one created by {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB}) disperses it, ending the spell. Its area is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}.

Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. When you cast the spell, you can empower it with your own life force. You can choose to take 10, 20, or 30 Necrotic damage. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}. When you do so, the spell's damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for every 10 Necrotic damage you take, up to a maximum of {@dice 10d6}.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can move the fog up to 30 feet. A creature also makes a save against this spell when the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} moves into its space and when it enters the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} or ends its turn there. A creature makes this save only once per turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Exhume
entries: Choose an unoccupied 20-foot square on the ground within range. This spell causes one pile of Humanoid bones to rise out of the ground within that square. If you cast this spell within a burial place such as a graveyard, mausoleum, or barrow, {@dice 1d4} corpses or piles of bones are exhumed. The ground itself isn't disturbed by this spell; the bones simply appear out of the ground.

spell.name: Summon Frostwyrm

m.text: an object with the image of a frostwyrm engraved on it worth 500+ GP

entries: You call forth a Frostwyrm spirit. It manifests in an unoccupied space that you can see within range and uses the {@creature Frostwyrm Spirit|WarcraftRevised} stat block. The creature disappears when it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or when the spell ends.

The creature is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, the creature shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: Use the spell slot's level for the spell's level in the stat block.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The paladin casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}):

trait.name: Devotion Aura
entries: While in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the paladin, the paladin and its allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, provided the paladin doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The paladin makes two Crusader Strike attacks.

action.name: Crusader Strike
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Judgment
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 6}, range 60 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 3d8}) Radiant damage, and the next attack roll against the target before the start of the paladin's next turn has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

action.name: Hammer of Justice {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 14}, one creature the paladin can see within 30 feet. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage, and the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of the paladin's next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

entries: The paladin or one creature it can see within 30 feet regains 18 ({@dice 4d8}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries: Immediately after hitting a creature with a melee weapon attack, the paladin deals an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage to the target. If the target is a Fiend or Undead, the extra damage increases to 13 ({@dice 3d8}).

reaction.name: Divine Shield (1/Day)
entries: {@actTrigger} The paladin takes damage. {@actResponse} The paladin surrounds itself with a barrier of holy energy, reducing the triggering damage to 0. The paladin then has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Death Knight
Why?
entries: Death Knights in the lore do not have healing capabilities. I've changed their spell list to better reflect this.
Javelins, Longsword, Shield, Holy Symbol, and Priest Pack were removed in favor of Greatsword, Arcane Focus, and Explorer's Pack.
The Runeforging feature has had the following text added:
In addition, you can use the inscribed weapon as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} to cast spells from your {@filter Death Knight spell list|spells|class=Death Knight Revised (wow:r)}.
This was added due to the removal of the Holy Symbol from starting equipment.

Lost the Find Steed spell. Gained the Summon Deathcharger spell instead. It is the same as Find Steed, but the Otherwordly Steed is now called a Deathcharger and lost both the Fey & Celestial options (but still gains the new undead option from this class). It also receieved a +1 AC & +5 initial HP bonus. The new Druid spell Innervate is intentionally accounted for to prevent early access to a flying mount.
Added a new spell: {@spell Summon Frostwyrm|warcraftrevised}
